procedure: Name the source of the stimulus.
Describe the stimulus and operating environment.
Describe the expected system response.
Define a measurable response target.
Trace the scenario to architecture tactics and tests.
purpose: Convert vague quality goals into stimuli, environments, responses, and measurable response targets.

tailoring.heavy: Utility tree, scenario catalog, architecture evaluation, and quality test plan.
tailoring.light: Three to five priority scenarios per release.

title: Quality attribute scenarios
trigger: A requirement says fast, secure, available, modifiable, testable, or deployable without measurable context.

anti_patterns: Assuming redundancy alone proves availability.
Testing only the happy path.
checks: Failure modes have detection and response.
Recovery targets are measurable.
A failed dependency does not create an uncontrolled cascade.
procedure: Classify failure sources and affected services.
Define availability scenarios and RTO/RPO expectations.
Select tactics such as redundancy, heartbeat, ping/echo, exception handling, rollback, retry, or graceful degradation.
Test recovery paths and operational visibility.
purpose: Design for failure detection, recovery, repair, and controlled loss of service.

tailoring.heavy: Fault model, RTO/RPO, failover rehearsal, and recovery evidence.
tailoring.light: Critical dependency timeout, retry, and fallback tests.

title: Availability and recovery tactics
trigger: The system must continue or recover after component, network, dependency, or data-store failures.

anti_patterns: Treating deployment as an afterthought.
Making an irreversible data change without a recovery plan.
checks: A release has an immutable identity.
Rollback or forward recovery is defined.
Schema and interface changes are compatible or deliberately coordinated.
procedure: Identify deployment units and compatibility constraints.
Separate deployment from activation where useful.
Use versioning, migration compatibility, rollback or roll-forward tactics.
Verify the deployed artifact and its runtime configuration.
purpose: Make software changes installable, reversible, and independently verifiable.

tailoring.heavy: Progressive delivery, compatibility matrix, migration rehearsal, and release observability.
tailoring.light: Automated build, smoke test, and rollback checklist.

title: Deployability and safe rollout
trigger: A release changes code, configuration, schema, infrastructure, or service topology.

anti_patterns: Adding abstractions without a change scenario.
Allowing cross-layer or cross-context shortcuts.
checks: A likely change has a bounded impact area.
The architecture exposes where change work will occur.
procedure: List likely change sources and affected responsibilities.
Localize likely changes behind interfaces or encapsulation.
Reduce unnecessary coupling and dependency distance.
Evaluate the change scenario against the current architecture.
Track architecture debt when a short-term shortcut increases future cost.
purpose: Control the cost and blast radius of expected changes through responsibility, coupling, cohesion, indirection, and deferred binding.

tailoring.heavy: Change scenario suite, dependency analysis, and architecture debt backlog.
tailoring.light: Record change hotspots and protect one boundary.

title: Modifiability tactics
trigger: The system must absorb new requirements, replace dependencies, or support multiple variants.

anti_patterns: Optimizing a guessed bottleneck.
Using average latency while ignoring tail latency.
checks: Workload and measurement method are explicit.
Tests represent peak and representative demand.
Performance improvements do not violate consistency or security requirements.
procedure: Define performance scenarios and workload shape.
Identify resource demands and bottlenecks.
Choose tactics such as concurrency, scheduling, queueing, caching, replication, resource pooling, or prioritization.
Load-test the architecture and compare measured response to targets.
purpose: Meet timing and throughput goals by managing demand, resources, concurrency, and processing order.

tailoring.heavy: Capacity model, load profile, saturation tests, and production telemetry.
tailoring.light: Load test the critical path and set latency/error budgets.

title: Performance tactics and resource management
trigger: The system has throughput, latency, capacity, or resource-use requirements.

anti_patterns: Relying on the UI for authorization.
Treating security as a penetration test performed at the end.
checks: Every sensitive operation has an authorization decision.
Trust boundaries and failure behavior are documented.
Security controls have verification evidence.
procedure: Identify assets, actors, trust boundaries, and threats.
Define authentication, authorization, confidentiality, integrity, and accountability scenarios.
Select architectural tactics such as least privilege, isolation, validation, encryption, audit, and attack detection.
Trace controls to security tests and release evidence.
purpose: Protect data and operations through explicit threat, trust-boundary, access, and attack-response decisions.

tailoring.heavy: Threat model, secure architecture review, abuse cases, dependency analysis, and security test suite.
tailoring.light: Threat model critical flows and test access control.

title: Security as an architectural quality
trigger: The system handles valuable data, privileged operations, external input, or untrusted components.

anti_patterns: Making production code depend directly on unreplaceable infrastructure.
Using end-to-end tests to cover every internal rule.
checks: Important components can be tested without the whole system.
Failures identify the responsible boundary.
Tests are repeatable and observable.
procedure: Define testability scenarios.
Expose controlled interfaces and seams.
Separate test data and environments.
Use dependency substitution, record/replay, assertions, and deterministic clocks where appropriate.
Measure test execution time and diagnostic quality.
purpose: Design the system so faults can be exposed, components isolated, behavior observed, and tests executed repeatably.

tailoring.heavy: Architecture-level testability review and layered test strategy.
tailoring.light: Test critical boundaries with fakes and contract tests.

title: Testability as an architectural property
trigger: Testing is expensive, slow, flaky, or cannot isolate architectural behavior.

anti_patterns: Treating every requirement as equally architectural.
Discovering architecture drivers only after implementation.
checks: Every architecture driver has a source and measurable scenario.
Architecture review covers the highest-risk drivers.
procedure: Review business goals, requirements, constraints, and stakeholder concerns.
Classify requirements as irrelevant, potentially significant, or clearly significant.
Elicit missing scenarios and thresholds.
Record the significant requirements in a utility tree or equivalent structure.
Use them as drivers for architecture design and evaluation.
purpose: Find the subset of requirements that materially shapes architecture and make their trade-offs explicit.

tailoring.heavy: Utility tree, stakeholder workshop, scenario prioritization, and traceability.
tailoring.light: Mark architecture drivers in the backlog or requirement register.

title: Architecturally significant requirements
trigger: A requirement affects performance, availability, security, safety, deployability, modifiability, or system boundaries.

anti_patterns: Big-design-up-front without feedback.
Selecting patterns without tracing them to drivers.
checks: Each design iteration has a goal and evidence.
The result addresses the selected drivers.
Unresolved risks become experiments or decisions.
procedure: Choose the iteration goal and prioritize drivers.
Select the system element to decompose.
Identify relevant design concepts and tactics.
Instantiate structures and allocate responsibilities.
Record preliminary views and analyze the design against the iteration goal.
Repeat until risk and scope are sufficient for the next increment.
purpose: Iteratively derive architecture structures from quality attributes, functionality, constraints, and design concepts.

tailoring.heavy: Architecture iteration plan, design review, and documented trade-offs.
tailoring.light: Design just enough for the next vertical slice.

title: Attribute-Driven Design
trigger: The system has multiple quality drivers or a nontrivial architecture decision must be made before implementation.

anti_patterns: Architecture review as a presentation with no challenge.
Evaluating only structure while ignoring quality scenarios.
checks: Stakeholders participate in the evaluation.
Trade-offs and risks are recorded, not merely discussed.
Actions have owners and follow-up evidence.
procedure: Collect business drivers and quality scenarios.
Present the architecture and identify approaches.
Analyze scenarios to expose sensitivity points, trade-offs, and risks.
Record findings, priorities, and recommended actions.
Use a lightweight evaluation when full ATAM cost is not justified.
purpose: Reduce architecture risk before implementation by examining scenarios, tactics, trade-offs, and sensitivity points with stakeholders.

tailoring.heavy: ATAM or equivalent multi-stakeholder evaluation with risk backlog.
tailoring.light: Focused review of one risky quality attribute.

title: Architecture evaluation and ATAM
trigger: Competing architectures or high-impact quality trade-offs require a decision.

anti_patterns: Producing a diagram with no element definitions or rationale.
Allowing documentation and implementation to diverge.
checks: A reader can find the view needed for their decision.
Rationale explains why alternatives were rejected.
Architecture debt has evidence, owner, and planned treatment.
procedure: Choose views based on stakeholder uses.
Document the architecture, interfaces, behavior, and rationale.
Relate decisions to requirements and quality scenarios.
Inspect the code and dependencies for architecture debt hotspots.
Schedule debt reduction with normal delivery work.
purpose: Keep architecture usable and evolvable by documenting views, decisions, rationale, and debt hotspots.

tailoring.heavy: View catalog, mappings, interface package, active review, and debt analysis.
tailoring.light: Context diagram, key view, interface notes, and decision log.

title: Architecture documentation, rationale, and debt
trigger: A system has multiple stakeholders, non-obvious constraints, or architecture decisions likely to outlive the current team.

anti_patterns: Using one overloaded diagram for every concern.
Mixing logical layers, runtime tiers, and deployment nodes without a mapping.
checks: The view answers a named stakeholder question.
Every symbol and relation has a defined meaning.
procedure: Identify the concern and intended use.
Choose module, component-and-connector, or allocation viewtype.
Define elements, relations, properties, and notation.
Connect the view to supporting catalogs and other views.
purpose: Describe different architectural concerns with a viewtype whose elements, relations, properties, and notation are explicit.

tailoring.heavy: View catalog with style guide, element catalog, mappings, and review checklist.
tailoring.light: Use one focused view per architecture question.

title: Architecture viewtypes and styles
trigger: A stakeholder needs to understand a structural, runtime, deployment, implementation, or work-assignment concern.

anti_patterns: Treating a style name as an architecture without defining its semantics.
Assuming layers and deployment tiers are interchangeable.
checks: The selected style does not imply unsupported behavior.
Relations have direction and ownership where relevant.
procedure: Select a style that matches the reasoning task.
Define the permitted elements and relations.
Document constraints and interpretation rules.
Provide examples and mappings to other styles.
purpose: Use established styles to communicate decomposition, dependency, runtime interaction, deployment, implementation, and work assignment.

tailoring.heavy: Style-specific notation, rules, examples, and consistency checks.
tailoring.light: Use layered, client-server, publish-subscribe, or deployment views only when they answer a decision.

title: Module, component-connector, and allocation styles
trigger: The architecture requires a shared vocabulary for structure, behavior, runtime interaction, or environment mapping.

anti_patterns: Using class structure as a substitute for runtime behavior.
Drawing sequence diagrams without stating protocol constraints.
checks: The behavior model covers normal and exceptional paths.
Ordering and timeout assumptions are explicit.
procedure: Identify externally visible stimuli and responses.
Choose statecharts, sequence diagrams, use cases, message charts, or formal/trace notation.
Document ordering, timing, error, and timeout constraints.
Link behavior to components, interfaces, requirements, and tests.
purpose: Record behavior, protocols, timing, ordering, and state transitions that cannot be understood from static structure alone.

tailoring.heavy: Behavior package with formal constraints and executable acceptance scenarios.
tailoring.light: Behavior diagram for each high-risk scenario.

title: Documenting architectural behavior
trigger: Correctness, concurrency, real-time behavior, failure handling, or protocol use matters.

anti_patterns: Generating a standard view set without stakeholder demand.
Combining unrelated views until neither concern is clear.
checks: Each view has an audience and intended use.
Documentation cost is justified by a decision or activity.
procedure: List stakeholders and the decisions they must make.
List anticipated uses: analysis, development, review, implementation, deployment, maintenance, or reconstruction.
Choose viewtypes and styles that support those uses.
Avoid views that no stakeholder will use.
Revisit the set when the architecture or audience changes.
purpose: Select only the views that have a real stakeholder use, balancing documentation benefit against maintenance cost.

tailoring.heavy: Usage matrix, view catalog, view packets, and periodic usefulness review.
tailoring.light: Context, module, runtime, and deployment views for the main decisions only.

title: Usage-based view selection
trigger: Starting or revising an architecture documentation package.

anti_patterns: A diagram without a key, catalog, or mapping.
Writing documentation as a one-time delivery artifact.
checks: Readers can navigate from overview to detail and back.
Every depicted element has supporting definition.
Cross-view mappings are complete enough for the intended use.
procedure: Provide a system overview and context diagram.
For each view, document the primary presentation, element catalog, relations, properties, and rationale.
Document mappings across views.
Maintain glossary, constraints, assumptions, and known omissions.
Package information by stakeholder use.
purpose: Build a coherent documentation package containing views, context, element catalogs, mappings, rationale, glossary, and completeness information.

tailoring.heavy: Stakeholder-specific view packets, complete catalogs, mappings, glossary, rationale, and review record.
tailoring.light: README, context diagram, key views, interface contracts, and decision records.

title: Architecture documentation package
trigger: An architecture must be built, reviewed, transferred, or maintained by people who were not present for its creation.

anti_patterns: Documenting only method signatures.
Leaking unstable implementation details as a promised contract.
checks: Consumers can use the interface without reading implementation.
Error and timeout behavior is documented.
Versioning and compatibility policy are explicit.
procedure: Identify the interface and its stakeholders.
Document signatures, data types, preconditions, postconditions, effects, errors, timing, and protocol ordering.
Document examples and version/evolution rules.
Expose only stable externally visible information.
Link interface documentation to tests and implementation.
purpose: Make software interfaces stable and usable by documenting syntax, semantics, protocols, assumptions, and externally visible behavior.

tailoring.heavy: Full interface package with semantic constraints, protocols, version policy, and compatibility tests.
tailoring.light: API schema, examples, errors, and contract tests.

title: Interface documentation
trigger: A component, service, database, message, or external system is consumed by another party.

anti_patterns: Proofreading diagrams without evaluating whether they support decisions.
Accepting documentation because the author understands it.
checks: Reviewers can answer their intended questions.
Findings have owners and closure evidence.
Documentation matches the current architecture.
procedure: Identify reviewers and their intended uses.
Review views, catalogs, mappings, interfaces, behavior, rationale, and glossary.
Check for conflicting definitions, missing elements, ambiguous notation, and stale assumptions.
Record findings and update the package.
purpose: Review architecture documentation for utility, correctness, completeness, consistency, and stakeholder usability.

tailoring.heavy: Active review with stakeholder walk-through and architecture/implementation comparison.
tailoring.light: Peer review against a view checklist.

title: Active architecture documentation review
trigger: An architecture package is proposed, baselined, or changed materially.

anti_patterns: Leaving configuration or dynamic behavior implicit.
Assuming all runtime variants receive equal validation.
checks: Variation is distinguishable from accidental implementation behavior.
Supported runtime states and transitions have tests or operational evidence.
procedure: Identify variation points and allowed values.
Document when and how variation is selected.
Document constraints, dependencies, and invalid combinations.
Describe runtime transitions and their impact on interfaces and deployment.
purpose: Record configured variation, runtime change, optional components, and dynamic behavior so architecture decisions remain explicit.

tailoring.heavy: Variability model, state model, compatibility matrix, and variant test plan.
tailoring.light: Configuration/feature-flag table and one dynamic behavior diagram.

title: Variability and dynamism documentation
trigger: A system supports plugins, configuration variants, dynamic binding, failover, hot deployment, or runtime reconfiguration.

anti_patterns: Adding layers or network hops by fashion.
Allowing dependencies to flow in every direction.
checks: Domain rules are not accidentally owned by the UI or persistence layer.
Distribution is justified by a measurable need.
procedure: Identify responsibilities and change forces.
Choose logical layers and dependency direction.
Keep layer interfaces explicit.
Deploy layers separately only when the operational benefit justifies the cost.
purpose: Separate presentation, domain, and data-source responsibilities to manage coupling while avoiding unnecessary distribution.

tailoring.heavy: Layer rules, dependency checks, interface package, and deployment rationale.
tailoring.light: Clear application/domain/data boundaries in one service.

title: Layering and responsibility boundaries
trigger: An application has multiple kinds of change, complex domain logic, or several clients of the same business behavior.

anti_patterns: Using a rich domain model for trivial CRUD.
Putting all business logic into a service layer because it is convenient.
checks: The choice explains domain complexity and future change.
The selected structure keeps business rules testable.
procedure: Assess domain complexity, rule interaction, number of clients, and expected change.
Use Transaction Script for simple procedural operations.
Use Domain Model for interacting rules and rich invariants.
Use Table Module where logic is organized around tabular data.
Add a thin Service Layer when clients need a stable application boundary.
purpose: Choose Transaction Script, Domain Model, Table Module, or Service Layer according to domain complexity and collaboration needs.

tailoring.heavy: Explicit domain-logic decision record and architecture tests.
tailoring.light: Start simple and promote structure when rule interaction justifies it.

title: Choosing an organization for domain logic
trigger: A team is deciding where business rules and use-case orchestration belong.

anti_patterns: Assuming an ORM removes mapping and performance decisions.
Letting persistence annotations dictate the domain model by accident.
checks: Persistence mapping does not silently change domain invariants.
Queries and transaction boundaries are observable and tested.
procedure: Identify ownership of persistence behavior.
Choose Gateway, Active Record, or Data Mapper based on domain complexity and coupling tolerance.
Define transaction and query boundaries.
Profile mapping and query behavior.
Keep schema evolution and mapping changes reviewable.
purpose: Isolate relational persistence choices from domain behavior and choose a mapping strategy appropriate to schema and object complexity.

tailoring.heavy: Explicit mapping strategy, query tests, migration plan, and performance profile.
tailoring.light: Repository/mapper with integration tests.

title: Relational data-source patterns
trigger: Domain objects must be persisted to a relational database or an existing schema.

anti_patterns: Hiding database calls inside arbitrary property access.
Using a unit of work without a clear transaction boundary.
checks: All intended changes commit or roll back coherently.
Lazy loading does not create unbounded query cascades.
procedure: Define business transaction scope.
Track new, dirty, and deleted objects.
Use identity mapping where object identity matters.
Apply lazy loading only where access patterns justify it.
Test commit, rollback, duplicate loading, and query count behavior.
purpose: Coordinate persistence changes, prevent duplicate in-memory identities, and control data loading inside a business transaction.

tailoring.heavy: Unit-of-work policy, identity rules, query budgets, and failure tests.
tailoring.light: Explicit transaction service and focused integration tests.

title: Unit of Work, Identity Map, and Lazy Load
trigger: A business operation changes multiple persistent objects or repeated loads create consistency/performance problems.

anti_patterns: Using a lock without defining its scope and failure behavior.
Confusing database transaction success with business transaction completion.
checks: Concurrent updates cannot silently overwrite valid changes.
Conflict outcomes are deterministic and actionable.
procedure: Identify business and system transaction boundaries.
Choose isolation, immutability, optimistic or pessimistic locking, or coarse-grained locking.
Define conflict detection and user/system recovery.
Test contention, rollback, retry, and deadlock behavior.
purpose: Protect business transactions from lost updates, inconsistent reads, deadlocks, and cross-session conflicts.

tailoring.heavy: Contention model, lock policy, retry/compensation design, and load tests.
tailoring.light: Database constraint or optimistic version check for the critical entity.

title: Concurrency and transaction patterns
trigger: Multiple requests can update the same business data or a business transaction spans separate system transactions.

anti_patterns: Distributing fine-grained objects for convenience.
Storing sensitive or large state in an uncontrolled client.
checks: State survives the required failures.
Remote calls have documented latency and error behavior.
Distribution reduces a real constraint rather than adding accidental coupling.
procedure: Classify state as client, server, database, or domain state.
Define ownership, lifetime, sensitivity, and failover requirements.
Keep remote interfaces coarse-grained and explicit.
Prefer local calls until distribution has a measured benefit.
Test restart, failover, serialization, and timeout behavior.
purpose: Choose where state lives and where distribution occurs based on failover, payload, latency, consistency, and operational constraints.

tailoring.heavy: Session failover policy, remote facade, DTO contract, and resilience tests.
tailoring.light: Stateless service plus explicit client/session identifier.

title: Session state and distribution boundaries
trigger: A web or service application needs user/session state or is considering remote calls.

anti_patterns: Putting transaction and pricing rules in controllers.
Returning persistence objects as an accidental public API.
checks: Presentation changes do not alter domain rules accidentally.
Input, application, and domain errors are distinguishable.
procedure: Separate input parsing and validation from application commands.
Choose Page Controller, Front Controller, MVC, Template View, or Application Controller as appropriate.
Keep presentation models distinct from domain models when needed.
Test controller routing, validation, and response behavior.
purpose: Separate request handling, presentation transformation, application flow, and domain behavior so UI changes do not corrupt business rules.

tailoring.heavy: Explicit presentation/application/domain boundaries and contract tests.
tailoring.light: Thin controller and application service with request/response DTOs.

title: Web presentation and controller boundaries
trigger: An application exposes browser or API clients with multiple flows or presentation forms.

anti_patterns: Creating repositories for every table without domain meaning.
Returning mutable persistence internals across boundaries.
checks: Query intent is testable without relying on incidental SQL.
Repository boundaries do not hide expensive unbounded reads.
procedure: Define aggregate or entity access boundaries.
Use Repository for domain collection semantics.
Use Query Object for composable query intent.
Keep mapping metadata and repository behavior testable.
Separate read models when query needs differ from write models.
purpose: Provide domain-oriented access to persisted objects while keeping query intent and mapping metadata explicit.

tailoring.heavy: Query objects, read models, mapping tests, and performance budgets.
tailoring.light: Repository only around aggregate boundaries.

title: Repository, Query Object, and metadata mapping
trigger: Consumers need collection-like access, complex queries, or multiple persistence implementations.

anti_patterns: Remoting every domain object method.
Returning internal persistence structures as DTOs.
checks: Remote call count and payload size meet performance goals.
Consumers are not coupled to internal domain object graphs.
procedure: Identify a complete business operation rather than exposing fine-grained objects.
Define a coarse-grained facade.
Shape DTOs for the consumer contract.
Version and test the remote contract.
Document timeout, error, and compatibility behavior.
purpose: Reduce network round trips and stabilize remote contracts by exposing coarse-grained operations and explicit transfer data.

tailoring.heavy: Versioned facade, schema evolution policy, compatibility suite, and telemetry.
tailoring.light: Stable API DTOs and contract tests.

title: Remote Facade and Data Transfer Object
trigger: A service must be consumed across a process or network boundary.

anti_patterns: Mocking every internal object instead of isolating true boundaries.
Representing money with primitive arithmetic without rounding policy.
checks: External failures are testable without requiring the real service.
Value objects enforce domain invariants.
Substitution does not change the intended contract.
procedure: Identify external or volatile dependencies.
Wrap them behind Gateway or Mapper interfaces.
Use Value Objects for domain concepts such as money and ranges.
Use Service Stub or Plugin to isolate tests and configuration.
Test the boundary and the domain behavior independently.
purpose: Isolate external resources and stabilize reusable concepts through Gateway, Mapper, Value Object, Money, Special Case, Plugin, and Service Stub patterns.

tailoring.heavy: Contract tests, failure simulation, plugin policy, and monetary correctness tests.
tailoring.light: Stub external services and use domain value objects for critical concepts.

title: Base patterns for isolation and testing
trigger: Code depends on external services, configuration, money, null cases, or replaceable implementations.

anti_patterns: Assuming all faults can be predicted and eliminated before release.
Treating operations as someone else's concern.
checks: Feature completion is separate from production readiness.
Recovery and diagnostic behavior have owners and evidence.
procedure: List expected production stresses and unknown failure modes.
Define how the system detects, contains, and recovers from failure.
Expose enough state for operators and developers to diagnose behavior.
Test production-readiness scenarios before release.
purpose: Treat production behavior, failure recovery, and operability as design concerns rather than post-development surprises.

tailoring.heavy: Failure model, recovery objectives, operational runbook, and resilience tests.
tailoring.light: Production-readiness checklist for critical paths.

title: Production readiness and recovery mindset
trigger: A feature is functionally complete but must face real users, traffic, dependencies, and failures.

anti_patterns: Synchronous chains without timeouts.
Unbounded resource use.
Many clients depending on one fragile service.
Retries that amplify load.
checks: Each critical dependency has bounded time, resources, and failure behavior.
A single failure cannot consume all shared capacity.
procedure: Map integration points and dependency chains.
Find shared bottlenecks, blocked threads, unbounded queues/results, cascading failures, and force multipliers.
Trace what happens when each dependency slows, fails, or returns invalid data.
Replace or isolate the amplification path.
purpose: Identify designs that amplify small faults into outages before they reach production.

tailoring.heavy: Dependency graph, fault injection, capacity model, and resilience review.
tailoring.light: Review critical calls for timeout, bounded resources, and fallback.

title: Stability anti-pattern detection
trigger: Reviewing a distributed or high-load design.

anti_patterns: Infinite waits.
One global thread pool for unrelated workloads.
Returning successful-looking data after a failed dependency.
checks: Timeouts are finite and observable.
Open/closed circuit behavior is tested.
Resource pools and queues are bounded.
Fallback does not claim a false success.
procedure: Set explicit timeouts for every remote or blocking operation.
Use circuit breaking to stop calls to a failing dependency.
Partition resources with bulkheads so one workload cannot exhaust all capacity.
Fail fast when continuing cannot produce a valid result.
Define fallback or degraded behavior where the business allows it.
purpose: Contain failures and prevent slow or broken dependencies from consuming the entire system.

tailoring.heavy: Circuit metrics, bulkheads by workload, load shedding, and failure tests.
tailoring.light: Timeout and bounded pool for critical dependency.

title: Stability patterns: timeouts, circuit breakers, bulkheads, and fail-fast
trigger: A service calls remote, slow, unreliable, or resource-constrained dependencies.

anti_patterns: Accepting every request until all queues and threads are exhausted.
Hiding overload behind retries.
checks: Overload produces controlled rejection or delay, not unbounded growth.
Critical operations retain capacity.
Users receive an honest status.
procedure: Define normal operating rate and safe capacity.
Measure queue depth, latency, saturation, and rejection.
Apply back pressure to producers or shed lower-value work.
Use governors or admission control for expensive operations.
Preserve critical traffic while rejecting work explicitly.
purpose: Keep demand and capacity within safe operating ranges instead of allowing overload to create collapse.

tailoring.heavy: Admission control, priority classes, capacity policy, and overload tests.
tailoring.light: Bounded queue and explicit busy response.

title: Steady state, back pressure, and load shedding
trigger: Traffic can exceed processing capacity or downstream services can slow.

anti_patterns: Logging without correlation or version identity.
A health endpoint that reports alive while dependencies are unusable.
Manual production changes with no audit.
checks: Operators can identify instance, version, configuration, and dependency state.
Health signals distinguish ready from merely alive.
Control actions are reversible or have a recovery path.
procedure: Expose health, readiness, dependency, configuration, and version information.
Provide structured logs, metrics, and correlation identifiers.
Provide safe operational controls such as drain, restart, disable, or traffic shift.
Keep control actions audited and bounded.
purpose: Make running instances inspectable and controllable so failures can be diagnosed and mitigated without code changes.

tailoring.heavy: Full telemetry, dashboards, runbooks, audited control plane, and fault drills.
tailoring.light: Versioned health/readiness endpoints and structured request IDs.

title: Operational transparency and control
trigger: A service runs across multiple instances, hosts, containers, or environments.

anti_patterns: Treating a load balancer as a complete availability solution.
Unbounded connection creation or stale service locations.
checks: Traffic does not route to known-unhealthy instances.
Discovery failure has bounded behavior.
Routing and capacity assumptions are documented.
procedure: Define service identity and discovery source.
Choose load-balancing and routing behavior.
Handle unhealthy instances and connection limits.
Test traffic shift, instance loss, network delay, and stale discovery.
purpose: Design the connections between instances so traffic distribution, discovery, and failure handling remain controlled.

tailoring.heavy: Failure-domain-aware routing, discovery tests, and capacity controls.
tailoring.light: Health-aware load balancing and bounded client connections.

title: Interconnect, load balancing, and service discovery
trigger: A system has multiple instances, dynamic capacity, or service-to-service calls.

anti_patterns: Editing production configuration manually.
Deploying code without knowing the active configuration.
checks: A deployment can reproduce the intended version and configuration.
Invalid configuration fails before damaging production.
Control-plane changes are auditable.
procedure: Separate code, configuration, and secrets.
Version configuration and validate it before activation.
Automate provisioning, deployment, and rollback.
Expose current configuration and control state.
Test control-plane failure separately from data-plane failure.
purpose: Manage deployment, configuration, provisioning, and operational control as software with explicit ownership and visibility.

tailoring.heavy: Infrastructure as code, progressive deployment, config validation, and control-plane observability.
tailoring.light: Versioned configuration and automated smoke deployment.

title: Control plane and configuration management
trigger: A system spans many instances, environments, versions, or operational services.

anti_patterns: Adding security checks only before launch.
Treating successful authentication as sufficient authorization.
checks: Sensitive operations have authorization and audit evidence.
Secrets are not embedded in code or logs.
Vulnerability response has an owner and path.
procedure: Identify sensitive data and trust boundaries.
Apply least privilege and secure secret handling.
Validate input and protect data integrity.
Monitor and respond to suspicious behavior and vulnerabilities.
Review security after changes and incidents.
purpose: Treat security, data protection, least privilege, and vulnerability response as continuous responsibilities.

tailoring.heavy: Security lifecycle, dependency scanning, incident response, and periodic review.
tailoring.light: Threat review and access tests for critical paths.

title: Security as an ongoing production process
trigger: The system handles user data, privileged operations, external input, or third-party dependencies.

anti_patterns: Large manual release windows.
Untested rollback.
Treating deployment completion as user-facing success.
checks: The same process works repeatedly across environments.
Deployment failure stops or rolls back safely.
Post-deployment checks verify behavior, not just process completion.
procedure: Package immutable artifacts.
Automate environment preparation and verification.
Use staged rollout, traffic control, or canary where risk warrants.
Separate deployment from activation when useful.
Automate rollback or roll-forward and verify the result.
purpose: Make deployment frequent, repeatable, observable, and reversible to reduce release risk.

tailoring.heavy: Progressive delivery, deployment telemetry, rollback rehearsal, and release audit.
tailoring.light: Automated deploy plus smoke test and rollback checklist.

title: Deployment automation and continuous delivery
trigger: A team must release changes regularly or recover from a failed deployment.

anti_patterns: Breaking consumers without notice.
Assuming all services deploy atomically.
checks: Consumer impact is known.
Old and new versions coexist safely during migration.
Deprecation has a date and owner.
procedure: Identify consumers and compatibility obligations.
Prefer additive compatible changes.
Version or deprecate breaking changes explicitly.
Test old and new consumers during transition.
Remove compatibility only after migration evidence.
purpose: Evolve services, interfaces, schemas, and dependencies without forcing synchronized failure across consumers.

tailoring.heavy: Compatibility matrix, dual-read/write migration, deprecation policy, and rollout telemetry.
tailoring.light: Contract tests and additive schema change.

title: Version and compatibility management
trigger: An API, schema, message, configuration, or dependency changes while consumers remain active.

anti_patterns: Testing only individual features under ideal conditions.
Running destructive experiments without a hypothesis or rollback.
checks: Tests reveal failure modes before production.
Recovery and user-visible behavior are measured.
Experiments have a safety boundary and abort condition.
procedure: Define stability hypotheses and measurable success criteria.
Test representative load and saturation.
Inject dependency, process, network, configuration, and deployment failures in a controlled environment.
Verify alerts, fallback, recovery, and data correctness.
Promote proven experiments into regression checks.
purpose: Validate stability and recovery behavior under realistic load, dependency failure, deployment change, and user demand.

tailoring.heavy: Staged resilience experiments, chaos program, and recurring recovery drills.
tailoring.light: Critical-path load and dependency-failure tests before release.

title: Production-oriented testing and failure simulation
trigger: A system has high availability, high traffic, or costly failure consequences.

anti_patterns: Adding a large framework before proving the constraint.
Optimizing one layer while ignoring the system.
checks: Adaptation is driven by evidence.
Architecture and operational changes have owners and follow-up measures.
procedure: Observe demand, incidents, capacity, and change cost.
Identify which architectural or process assumption is now limiting.
Make a small reversible improvement.
Measure the result and feed it into the next decision.
purpose: Evolve people, process, architecture, and information flow together as demand, scale, and failure evidence change.

tailoring.heavy: Architecture evolution roadmap and organizational feedback loops.
tailoring.light: Retrospective action tied to one measurable pain.

title: Adaptive architecture and feedback
trigger: The system or its environment changes faster than initial assumptions remain valid.

anti_patterns: Treating chaos as random destruction.
Running experiments before basic monitoring and recovery exist.
checks: Steady state is measurable before the experiment.
Blast radius and abort conditions are explicit.
Findings create remediation and regression evidence.
procedure: Define steady-state behavior and user-impact measure.
Form a failure hypothesis.
Run the smallest safe experiment in an appropriate environment.
Observe impact, stop if safety limits are crossed, and analyze results.
Fix the weakness and repeat the experiment.
purpose: Discover systemic weaknesses by deliberately introducing controlled failures and checking whether steady-state expectations hold.

tailoring.heavy: Production-safe chaos program with governance, blast-radius controls, and recurring experiments.
tailoring.light: Staged dependency-failure experiment in preproduction.

title: Chaos engineering as hypothesis-driven validation
trigger: The system has established observability, safe abort controls, and a resilience hypothesis worth testing.

anti_patterns: Combining requirements, architecture, test plans, and project plans in one document.
Treating screenshots or solution choices as a substitute for functional and data requirements.
Leaving unresolved TBD items for developers to guess during implementation.
checks: The SRS lets developers and testers determine required behavior without guessing.
Every requirement has a stable ID and does not mix independent behaviors.
Quality requirements are quantitative or explicitly unresolved decisions.
Design, implementation, test-plan, and project-plan detail is excluded except for justified constraints.
procedure: Choose a project-appropriate SRS structure and define version, scope, readers, references, and ID conventions.
Organize atomic functional requirements and link their evidence, models, rules, and acceptance scenarios.
Specify logical data, external-interface, quality, constraint, assumption, and dependency requirements.
Keep requirements traceable, stable-ID based, cross-linked, and free of duplicated content.
Baseline each selected increment only after open issues are resolved, deferred, or explicitly decided by an accountable owner.
purpose: Organize the behavior, qualities, constraints, data, and external-interface needs of one product or increment into a versioned requirements baseline that supports downstream work without dictating an internal solution.

tailoring.heavy: System and subsystem SRS baselines with requirements management repository, formal inspection, and version/change history.
tailoring.light: Versioned increment SRS assembled from linked requirement cards, scenarios, models, and open decisions.

title: Software requirements specification as an implementation-independent baseline
trigger: A project needs a technical requirement baseline for an increment, multiple readers need a consistent source of truth, or requirement cards/models are too distributed to serve downstream work.
